findings.title: First generated packet can adopt another checkout and clear the current blocker
findings.diagnosis: requireApprovedRepository checks the approved base and compares roots only with an earlier HMA packet. On a legacy run with no packet, a clone containing that base becomes the root anchor. The independent probe commits a different artifact in the clone, imports a receipt-bound pass, removes the unit BLOCK and satisfies the host review gate. No hostile same-UID process, forged receipt, stage approval or route substitution is required. This violates architecture §7.1 correct repository/revision identity and Gate C exact-current-target snapshot semantics. The comment that accepted-plan root binding is Gate D describes the implementation limit; it does not make a different-target resolution safe. A final stage transition on the original checkout was not demonstrated and is not claimed.

evidence.observation: No prior packet means the root-comparison loop supplies no approved-root check; VerifyBase only establishes that the commit exists in the candidate checkout.
TestAuditor8JFirstPacketCloneRoot records APPROVE, an empty findings snapshot and gate=<nil> for a distinct clone artifact.
Retains the original checkout, distinct clone checkout, core/host chains, packet, report and receipt. The earlier core record contains prior/BLOCK. The final snapshot has no findings.

fix.action: Bind a trusted canonical repository root or equivalent repository identity before the first review-packet dispatch. Compare it at packet generation, review import and findings import. For legacy runs without such a binding, refuse authoritative import until an explicit trusted migration records the intended root. Do not take that binding from the first candidate packet itself.
fix.why: A separately established identity closes the unanchored first-packet path while keeping the approved-base and live-artifact checks.

verification.method: Repeat TestAuditor8JFirstPacketCloneRoot with the same-base clone and a distinct committed artifact. Fingerprint both chains. Also try a different base and a later alternate root.
verification.expected: Every wrong target refuses before a usable packet/import/snapshot; BLOCK and both chains stay unchanged.

verification.method: Generate and import an exact independent report for the recorded approved root, then its findings snapshot.
verification.expected: The current own-unit control can resolve findings and satisfy only the host review gate.

fix.tradeoffs: Legacy runs need a visible trusted migration. Canonical paths must distinguish approved linked worktrees/clones according to the chosen identity contract. Existing active approvals must not be silently rebound.
fix.alternative: Until an approved root binding is available, make initial packet imports diagnostic-only and prohibit finding resolution and host-gate satisfaction.

findings.title: Slash-separated finding IDs collide across exact unit owners
findings.diagnosis: UnitFindingID concatenates unit + "/" + source ID without escaping. Unit U1/sub with finding F and unit U1 with finding sub/F both become U1/sub/F. SnapshotFindings preserves both owners and the store accepts duplicate global IDs. The independent probe passes the resulting advisory-only state to the existing validator-contract evaluator, which refuses DUPLICATE_FINDING_ID. This is a finding-model integration and resolution-identity defect. No cross-unit BLOCK deletion was observed.

evidence.observation: Tuple encoding is ambiguous; preserving a different owner and adding a colliding imported finding creates two identical ID values.
TestAuditor8JCrossUnitSlashCollision stores two ADVISORY/PARK findings owned by U1/sub and U1; validator evaluation returns REJECTED/DUPLICATE_FINDING_ID.
Retains packet, report, receipt and both committed chains for the colliding snapshot.

fix.action: Use an unambiguous encoding of the (unit ID, source finding ID) pair, or reject a global-ID collision before any snapshot append. Preserve original source IDs and migrate existing references and active waiver targets explicitly.
fix.why: Every finding must have one unambiguous identity in the core APIs that address findings by ID. UnitID ownership alone does not make global IDs unique.

verification.method: Repeat the end-to-end U1/sub+F and U1+sub/F fixture, including source IDs and unit IDs with multiple slashes.
verification.expected: Distinct findings have distinct core IDs, or the second import refuses without append. A supported advisory-only snapshot passes validator-contract evaluation.

verification.method: Re-run exact-owner preservation, legacy finding migration and active-waiver tests.
verification.expected: No other-unit finding, waiver or reference is silently dropped, reassigned or weakened.

fix.tradeoffs: Changing identifier encoding needs compatibility handling for existing reports, references and waivers. Rejection is smaller containment but does not support all otherwise-valid IDs.
fix.alternative: Restrict unit/source IDs to an explicit safe grammar at every creation and migration boundary, with visible handling of incompatible legacy IDs.

findings.title: Loop recapture can attach another repository artifact to an anchored unit
findings.diagnosis: loop-evidence verifies the envelope digest and hma store/run/unit fields. It does not compare the journal repo identity or caller repository root/base with the unit approval or an existing generated packet. After an ordinary packet anchors root A, the independent probe supplies a state naming A but requests recapture in repository B with B's base. HMA executes true in B and appends core and host evidence under A's unit. The record exposes B's working directory/head, so this is not a demonstrated concealed criterion credit. No PASSED criterion, lease, review approval or stage advancement results. It still fails the correct-target evidence integration boundary in architecture §7.1 and §14.

evidence.observation: Admission checks open run and approved route, then captures the caller root/base. State parsing binds hma identifiers but does not consume or validate repo.root/head.
TestAuditor8JLoopWrongTargetProbe succeeds on another root/base and records EVIDENCE_RECORDED; the test deliberately fails that outcome.
The loop-other-root-* subdirectory retains the source state and resulting core/host chains, including the evidence output artifact.

fix.action: Before execution, compare the journal repository identity and caller root/base with the independently established run/unit target. Reuse the approved base/root checks where available. On an unbound legacy run, refuse authoritative loop evidence until its intended repository identity is established.
fix.why: Fresh recapture proves what ran in the selected directory; it does not establish that this was the unit's intended artifact.

verification.method: Repeat TestAuditor8JLoopWrongTargetProbe with a correct journal/root control, wrong root, wrong approved base and same-base clone. Fingerprint both chains and use an execution marker.
verification.expected: Wrong-target cases refuse before executing argv or appending either chain. The exact current target recaptures successfully.

verification.method: Re-run terminal-lock, output retention, mutation refusal, envelope drift and no-criterion-credit controls.
verification.expected: Existing safe recapture behavior remains and no import credits a criterion.

fix.tradeoffs: The journal repository schema and allowed artifact evolution must be specified. A historical journal may be a lead for a new current check, but must not silently select another repository or claim historical check authority.
fix.alternative: Permit explicitly labelled diagnostic capture of a foreign artifact in a separate evidence namespace that cannot serve as this unit's required evidence.

limitations: Blinding breach: one command read Gate A v3 lines 47-66 (§2 lease text), outside the user-authorized §3-§4 and §6. The text supplied design constraints, not prior review verdicts. The audit therefore records isolation_compromised=true and isolation=compromised. No restart or nested agent was permitted. Reproductions remain inspectable; do not call this a fully isolated independent signoff.

The scope note was never read past line 86. A smaller sed range within 1-86 was used once in addition to the requested exact sed command. No TODO Gate C section, §4a+ scope material, forbidden prior audit directory or claude directory was read. The only prior-review input was the authorized criteria file.
Author comments and test names in the audited artifacts contain historical finding labels. They were treated as artifacts, not verdict evidence. No optional unblinding was performed.

Tests ran on Linux amd64 with go1.27.1 in a repository copy. The original repository was not edited. The initial freeze also hashed ignored audit-scope files as requested, but their contents were not audited.

Initial go test and -race failed one dogfood-helper test because the execution copy is under /tmp. Setting TMPDIR to an audit-owned child directory makes its non-scratch-repository assumption hold; the complete suite and race run then pass. Both failed and corrected logs are retained.

Initial own snapshot assertion used an ID-only map and falsely reported that a preserved other-unit BLOCK was gone. Raw-state inspection showed both entries remained. The assertion was corrected to key by owner and ID. The actual duplicate-ID defect was then reproduced separately. Initial logs are retained.

One reproduction-retention retry failed when overwriting an earlier read-only Git object copy. The fixture had already produced APPROVE and an empty snapshot. Retention now uses a fresh directory; final logs include complete retained artifacts and the intended assertions.
Baseline helper first build failed VCS stamping in an archive without .git. Building with -buildvcs=false succeeded. The helper only writes labelled synthetic scratch records.

No production run, real human approval, external model API or nested agent CLI was used. Test route facts, receipts and approval-shaped records are labelled synthetic fixture evidence; they are not authentic human authority.

No real verify-loop controller/worker launch was run. Its current validated route contract requires agent-dispatch, which the audit forbids nesting. Contract-shaped journal fixtures test HMA ingestion and recapture; genuine controller end-to-end behavior is not certified.

The host-written receipt boundary is trusted for accident/drift detection. This audit makes no same-UID adversary or arbitrary-program shell-execution guarantee. Wrappers/shebang entry-point refusal does not prove that an allowed executable never launches a shell internally.

Gate D acceptance-contract inputs, reservation/namespace reconciliation, lease generation, actual kernel/budget reproduction and independent criterion-credit pairs are human-deferred and were not counted as implemented Gate C successes.
Jev was absent from available host tools. The recorded fallback is the auditor/human decision path. No other model was represented as Jev.
The negative controls intentionally produce failing tests for J8-01, J8-02 and J8-03. Proposed fixes were not implemented or validated.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Generated immutable review packet binds current unit implementation, exact repository/head/diff/worktree, current core state, approved route and plan, current findings/waivers, unique nonce and dispatch; rejects caller packet impersonation.
gate_c_requirements.observation: Packet generation, nonce, core-state and approved-base checks work. The first packet can adopt a clone with a different head and diff. Its report removes the current unit BLOCK. J8-01.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Receipt and report import binds exact completed successful review run, ledger namespace/root, launch artifact, worker/provider/model/effort, report bytes and HMA nonce; refuses stale/missing/wrong/rewritten reports without append.
gate_c_requirements.observation: Exact successful run, launch values, report digest, nonce and route fields are checked. Wrong or absent receipt fields refuse without chain changes. Full namespace admission is explicitly Gate D.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Strict audit report validation preserves Python contract semantics for keys, Unicode, UTF-8, structural and approving consistency; no invalid report approves or clears blockers.
gate_c_requirements.observation: Malformed, incomplete, contradictory, case-variant, Unicode-fold, control-separator and invalid UTF-8 inputs do not approve or clear BLOCK. Python contract checks agree on the tested report fixtures. Exhaustive Unicode whitespace parity also passes.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Reviewer independence covers every retained implementation; normal model/context/worker separation and high-risk/disputed/final provider/model family separation; approving final isolation is isolated.
gate_c_requirements.observation: Executed route tests reject self/model/context reuse, earlier retained implementers, and same-family final/high/disputed routes. Final pass requires isolated report. These are deterministic checks over host-declared route facts.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Only latest, unused, current-core, current-artifact review can snapshot and satisfy host gate; pending dispatch or newer evidence invalidates stale approval; concurrent replay fails closed.
gate_c_requirements.observation: One concurrent import succeeds. Replay fails. A newer unanswered packet closes the gate. The new valid final report and snapshot reopen it. Core drift and live artifact drift refuse.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Failed/escalated snapshot preserves existing BLOCK and WAIVABLE findings including same IDs; current authentic approving snapshot may resolve exact owned unit only; imports never credit criterion PASSED.
gate_c_requirements.observation: Non-approving snapshots preserve exact-unit BLOCK and WAIVABLE findings. Approving snapshots preserve other owners. Imports credit no criterion. Slash-containing unit/finding pairs nevertheless create duplicate global IDs and fail validator evaluation. J8-02.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Legacy findings and waivers retain ownership and force; unknown ownership remains; legacy records readable and mode visible; migration to packet_import refuses new manual overrides.
gate_c_requirements.source: Gate C migration objective; architecture §7,§15; scope §1-3
gate_c_requirements.observation: A binary compiled from baseline HEAD wrote old finding and waiver records. Current code reads them. Own-unit approval resolves owned legacy findings. Other-unit and ambiguous findings remain. Active waiver survives. Modes and manual-packet refusal pass.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Review launches are bound to a short validity interval and frozen actual start time; before issuance, expiry or invalidation refuses, latest dispatch and replay checks are atomic.
gate_c_requirements.observation: Review launch interval is [record timestamp, record timestamp+1 hour). Before issuance, equality at expiry and after expiry refuse. Just before expiry passes, even when import occurs later. Core-head invalidation and once-only import checks work. Lease-generation and namespace reconciliation remain Gate D.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Verify-loop evidence validates envelope/store/run/unit/target and hashes, reruns explicit safe argv with no shell, retains exact output/digest/exit/truncation, appends only fresh nonmutating evidence, no criterion or lease authority.
gate_c_requirements.observation: Envelope/store/run/unit bindings, argv safety, self-recapture, immutable output, exit/truncation and corruption checks work. Journal repository identity and approved base are not checked against recapture input. An existing anchored run accepts another root/base. J8-03. No criterion credit was observed.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Terminal or missing runs refuse before check execution; concurrent core terminal append cannot precede admitted execution; core/host lock and chain guarantees remain.
gate_c_requirements.source: architecture §7.1,§15; task14 host store; Gate B regression objective
gate_c_requirements.observation: Missing and terminal runs refuse before execution. An admitted check holds the core lock. Concurrent direct terminal append waits and then fails its stale sequence. An open-run control succeeds. Gate B crash/chain/approval/terminal regression tests pass.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: End-to-end audit failure, linked repair and fresh verification work; stale/self review, malformed imports, gate bypass and migration negative controls reject; Gate B crash/concurrency/approval/terminal guarantees regressions absent.
gate_c_requirements.observation: Repository failure→repair→fresh review fixture and 17-check host dogfood pass. Independent controls pass. Three independent defect probes fail as expected. A real verify-loop worker/controller launch was not executed because the current route contract only permits agent-dispatch and nested agent CLIs are forbidden for this audit.

gate_c_requirements.requirement: Human-deferred reservation/reconciliation/lease-generation, contract-rich packet inputs, criterion credit, kernel/budget reproduction requirements remain recorded with unchanged exit tests and Gate D prerequisite; Gate C neither claims nor relies on them.
gate_c_requirements.source: human 2026-10-17 scope acceptance; scope §0.1; v3 §6, v6 §5, v7
gate_c_requirements.observation: Accepted §0.1 records reservation, replay/admission/consumption, namespace association, validity generations, criterion credit, reproduced dispositions and contract-rich packet inputs with Gate D exit tests. Current import paths make no PASSED criterion or bounded-execution/closure claim. Deferred items are not counted as Gate C implementation successes.

prior_findings.observation: Current packet carries core head, plan digest, criteria dispositions, findings and waiver scopes. Contract-rich standalone inputs and immutable source manifests remain Gate D by accepted §0.1.

prior_findings.observation: Baseline-written own-unit findings resolve; other-unit/ambiguous findings and active waiver remain. No owner is inferred from a string prefix.

prior_findings.observation: Reproduced dispositions and exact-target independent criterion-credit pairs remain Gate D. Current imports never write criterion PASSED.

prior_findings.observation: In-scope wrong envelope/store refusals and genuine recapture controls pass. Reservation/namespace/launch reconciliation matrix remains Gate D.

prior_findings.observation: Missing/terminal runs refuse before argv. Core lock covers admission, execution and append.

prior_findings.observation: Legacy and migrated modes are visible. Manual packet and fallback dispatch are refused after migration.

prior_findings.title: A newer unanswered packet does not invalidate an older approving review
prior_findings.observation: Pending newer final packet invalidates earlier pass; authentic current final receipt/report/snapshot restores host gate. Concurrent duplicate imports refuse.

prior_findings.title: The fixed review packet still omits mandatory review inputs
prior_findings.observation: Standalone immutable request/criteria/non-goal/budget/evidence/policy inputs depend on the acceptance contract; accepted §0.1 preserves Gate D exit tests.

prior_findings.observation: Lennon explicitly accepted §0.1 on 2026-10-17. Deferred proof rows remain named with Gate D exit tests; no Gate D success is inferred.

prior_findings.title: Legacy dispatch input can impersonate an HMA-generated review packet
prior_findings.observation: Caller Packet binding is refused before append in legacy and migrated runs. Real generated packet/import control works.

prior_findings.title: Loop recapture discards the verification output
prior_findings.observation: Both streams, framed digest, exit 7 and explicit output cap survive process exit; intact artifact reuse succeeds. Mutation refusal is covered by repository fixture.

prior_findings.title: Go reads case-variant JSON keys that the Python contract ignores
prior_findings.observation: Exact-key decoder ignores ASCII/Unicode case-fold aliases in report, receipt, binding and loop structures. Case-variant passing verdict cannot override fix-required.

prior_findings.title: Go and Python disagree on required nonempty report fields
prior_findings.observation: Information separators fail nonempty checks. Exhaustive Python/Go whitespace comparison covers all 0x110000 code points.

prior_findings.title: Interrupted output-artifact writes are trusted as complete on retry
prior_findings.observation: Empty/partial/symlink residue refuses before chain append and remains intact. Correct pre-existing artifact is reused. Final name uses atomic link after write+sync.

prior_findings.title: loop-evidence executes a shell command from an imported journal
prior_findings.observation: Loop and direct capture refuse shell executable/wrapper/shebang entry points; unsafe verify-loop argv controls pass. Plain binary/data controls execute. Arbitrary approved program internals remain trusted.

prior_findings.title: Invalid UTF-8 report passes Go checks but fails the Python validator
prior_findings.observation: Invalid UTF-8 report, receipt and loop state refuse without approval or chain append.

prior_findings.title: The shell filter refuses a shell name used as plain data
prior_findings.observation: printf %s sh runs. Shell entry points remain refused.

prior_findings.title: Executable shell scripts and wrapper aliases bypass the no-shell kernel
prior_findings.observation: Direct shell/env shebangs, symlinked interpreters, env aliases and xargs shells refuse before execution. This does not prove arbitrary executables never launch a shell internally.

prior_findings.title: A concurrent trusted core terminal append can precede loop check execution
prior_findings.observation: Core lock probe sees LOCK_HELD. Direct terminal append cannot commit during capture and its stale sequence is refused afterward.

prior_findings.title: A review with a different approved base can clear the current unit blocker
prior_findings.observation: Wrong base and later alternate/clone roots refuse. First packet still adopts another clone/head and clears BLOCK. The code records an initial-root limitation, but that does not enforce correct-target finding resolution. J8-01.
